title: The women who funded him (Luke 8:1–3)
hook: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others ministered to him of their substance

segments.voice: Yesterday, an alabaster jar at Simon's dinner, and a woman who loved much. Your line was go in peace.

Here's a question the Gospels rarely stop to answer: who paid for all this? Jesus and twelve men walking from town to town for months, not fishing, not farming, not working for wages. Somebody bought the bread, the sandals, the oil, a roof when there was one. Most of the time the Gospels skip the budget. Luke doesn't. In three short verses, tucked between bigger stories, he tells us who kept the whole mission going.
screen: `WHO PAID FOR ALL THIS?` → `THIRTEEN MEN, NO WAGES.` → `THREE VERSES WITH THE ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Jesus went through the cities and towns preaching the kingdom, Luke says, and the twelve were with him, and certain women. Then he names them. Mary, called Magdalene, out of whom seven devils had gone. Joanna, wife of Chusa, Herod's steward: married to the man who managed the household of the king who would later mock Jesus. Susanna, about whom we know nothing else at all. And "many others who ministered unto him of their substance." Their substance means their own money and goods. These women weren't just along for the ride. They were paying for it. Ministered is worth stopping on. In Greek it's diakoneo, to serve, the same root that gives the Church the word deacon. Now follow these women forward. Luke says the women who had followed him from Galilee stood at a distance and watched the crucifixion, and saw where he was laid. On Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene and Joanna are named among the women who found the tomb empty and told the apostles. The ones who funded the road were still there at the end. In 2016 Pope Francis raised the memorial of Mary Magdalene to a feast, and the decree honored her with an old title: apostle to the apostles. Many parishes still run on people like Joanna and Susanna, often women, often unnamed: the ones who count the collection, wash the linens, teach the children, bring the casseroles. Luke wrote their names down.
screen: `MARY, JOANNA, SUSANNA, MANY OTHERS.` · `OF THEIR SUBSTANCE: THEIR OWN MONEY.` · `MINISTERED: THE DEACON WORD.` · `THE SAME WOMEN AT THE TOMB.` · then, large: `THEY MINISTERED OF THEIR SUBSTANCE.`

segments.voice: Picture the place you belong, a parish, a school, a team, a family, and look for the ones doing the work nobody announces: the one who unlocks the door, makes the coffee, keeps the list, remembers the birthdays. Pick one, and think of exactly what she gives. If you pray, thank God for her by name.
Mary Magdalene. Named first among the women who funded Jesus' mission out of their own means, and stayed to the end, even at the tomb. Today's word.
Your line: they ministered of their substance. Their own money and goods, spent on the road. That's day four hundred fifty-seven.

howItsDone: The Church keeps the feast of Saint Mary Magdalene on July 22, and in many Catholic parishes women carry much of the daily work: catechesis, sacristy care, charity, music and administration.

original.note: Greek: they were serving, from diakoneo, the root of deacon.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus' followers were twelve men.
what it means: Luke says many women traveled with him too and paid for the mission from their own means.
what a scholar hears: diakoneo, the deacon verb, used for women's service; the same women are witnesses of the cross, burial and empty tomb.

chat.says: Who paid for Jesus and the twelve to travel around for months?
options: Women did: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others, from their own means.
Luke says the twelve kept fishing on the side to pay for the road.
Luke says Herod's household paid, since the king wanted to meet him.
chat.meaning: Luke names women who ministered to Jesus of their substance, their own money and goods. The same women stood by at the cross and found the empty tomb.

diakoneo.meaning: Greek: to serve, the root of deacon

Susanna.meaning: named once by Luke; nothing else is known of her

substance.meaning: here: their own money and goods

sources.quoted: many others who ministered unto him of their substance

notes: Confirm Douay-Rheims wording of Luke 8:3 ('who ministered unto him of their substance').
Some manuscripts read 'ministered unto them' rather than 'unto him'; confirm the Douay reading.
2016: Pope Francis raised the memorial of Mary Magdalene to a feast; the decree used the title 'apostle of the apostles' (apostolorum apostola). Confirm.
Herod Antipas mocking Jesus is Luke 23:11; confirm 'the king' is acceptable shorthand for the tetrarch.
